title: One-Page Profile Display
strapline: A single sheet for each child — what we love about them, what matters to them, and how best to support them — so every adult starts from strengths.
intent: Children are known quickly and warmly by every adult — key person, supply staff, students — because their profile leads with who they are.
Children experience consistent support because 'how best to help me' is written down and shared, not held in one person's head.
Children see themselves celebrated: what people admire about them comes first, before any need or difficulty.
Children have their voice, preferences and communication needs honoured across the whole team.
Children benefit from a genuine home-setting partnership, because families co-author the profile.
implementation: Build each profile around three headings: 'what we love about you', 'what's important to you', and 'how best to support you' — strengths always first.
Co-create with the child and family — their words, their photos, their favourite things — so it's authentic, not a professional's summary.
Keep it to a single, readable page with a clear photo, so a new adult can absorb it in a minute before working with the child.
Display or store profiles where the team actually looks — the room folder, the changing area, the group-time basket — and point new staff to them.
Write the 'how to support me' section in concrete, doable terms: 'give me warning before transitions', 'I sign for more', not vague labels.
Review and refresh regularly, especially at transitions, so the profile grows with the child and never goes stale.
key_questions: What do you love doing best?
What helps you when you're feeling wobbly?
Who are the special people in your life?
What would you like new grown-ups to know about you?
Shall we add your new favourite thing to your page?

impact.text: Children build warm bonds with familiar and new adults who understand them from the start.
Children make real choices and know their ideas and preferences matter here.
Children have their feelings and calming strategies known and honoured by the team.
Children's communication — signs, symbols, words — is understood consistently by all adults.
Children take visible pride as adults notice and celebrate what they love and can do.

enhancements: A child-friendly version the child illustrates themselves, kept in their own tray.
A transition profile that travels to the next room or school, so knowledge isn't lost.
A quick-glance 'top three things to know' card for supply staff and students.
Regular family 'add to my page' invitations at pick-up, keeping it a living document.
A photo wall of every child's profile at their height, so children can find and talk about their own.

playing_exploring: Children help choose the photos and favourites that go on their page, exploring how they see themselves.
Talking around the profile invites children to share what they love and know.
active_learning: Being consistently understood and supported helps children engage and persist with confidence.
Children feel a strong sense of belonging that underpins their willingness to have a go.
creating_thinking: Children reflect on their own preferences, strengths and what helps them — early self-awareness.
They contribute their own ideas about how adults can best support them.
